title: 50 Swahili Phrases in 11 Minutes | Learn Swahili for Beginners (Hope)
description:
Learn 50 essential Swahili phrases in 11 minutes - the fun, fast way.
#Swahili #LearnSwahili #LanguageLearning

Every phrase follows the same rhythm: hear it in English, hear it in Kiswahili, then say it out loud with the pronunciation guide. Perfect for beginners, travellers and anyone who wants to speak Swahili with confidence.

WHAT YOU GET
- 8 themed chapters, 50 real-life phrases
- Kiswahili audio from a native voice
- English pronunciation guide for every line
- A brand-new lesson every single day

CHAPTERS
0:07  Hope · Tumaini
1:31  Strength · Nguvu
2:46  Courage · Ujasiri
4:04  Feelings & Emotions · Hisia na Machozi
5:28  Celebrations & Parties · Sherehe na Mikutano
7:00  Work & Office · Kazi na Ofisi
8:14  Love · Upendo
9:27  Common Native Slang · Lugha ya Mitaani ya Kawaida

PHRASE LIST

HOPE · Tumaini
• I’m choosing hope, even now. - Ninachagua tumaini, hata sasa.  [Ninachagua TA-maini, hata SA-sa.]
• My heart keeps looking forward. - Moyo wangu unaendelea kutazama mbele.  [MO-yo wangu u-naen-de-lea ku-taza-ma MBE-le.]
• Tomorrow still feels possible for me. - Kesho bado inawezekana kwangu.  [KE-sho ba-do i-na-we-ze-ka-na kwan-gu.]
• I can start again with hope. - Naweza kuanza upya kwa tumaini.  [Na-we-za ku-an-za u-PYA kwa TA-maini.]
• I’ll believe it gets better. - Nitaamini inakuwa bora.  [Ni-ta-a-mi-ni in-aku-wa bo-ra.]
• Even small progress gives me hope. - Maendeleo madogo yanayonipa tumaini.  [Ma-aen-de-le-o ma-do-go ya-na-ni-pa TA-maini.]
• I’m listening for good news. - Nasikiliza habari njema.  [Na-si-KI-li-za ha-bi-ri njE-ma.]

STRENGTH · Nguvu
• Focus on slow, steady strength. - Songa polepole, thabiti, kwa nguvu.  [SOnga polepole, THA biti, kwa NGUvu.]
• I lift, then I breathe. - Na kuinua, kisha napumua.  [Na KUinua, kiisha naPUMUA.]
• My core is getting stronger. - Tumbo langu la ndani linakuwa na nguvu.  [TUMbo langu la NDANI linakuwa na NGUvu.]
• One more rep, then relax. - Fanya marudio mengine, halafu pumzika.  [FA nya maRUDIO Mengine, halafu pumZIKA.]
• Strength grows when I persist. - Nguvu hukua ninapositiza.  [NGUvu huKUA niVYAPO sTi za.]
• I’m not giving up today. - Leo siiachii, naendelea tu.  [LEO siA chi i, naENdelea tu.]

COURAGE · Ujasiri
• I will face it, not run. - Nitaikabili, si kukimbia.  [Nita- KA bili, si ku-KIM bia.]
• My voice counts, even shaky. - Sauti yangu ina maana, hata nikiwa na hofu kidogo.  [SaaUti yangu i-NA maaNA, HATA nikiwa na hofu ki-DOGO.]
• I can be brave and still nervous. - Naweza kuwa jasiri na bado nina woga.  [Naa-weza kuwa JA si ri na ba-do ni-na WO ga.]
• I choose action over panic. - Nnachagua hatua kuliko hofu.  [NnA CHU a-ga HA ta-ku-lo-co huo-FU.]
• Today I’ll ask for what I need. - Leo nitaomba ninachohitaji.  [LEO ni-ta-O mba ni-na-CHO hI ta ji.]
• I’m allowed to start imperfectly. - Ninaruhusiwa kuanza bila kuwa kamili.  [Ni-na-RU hu si-wa ku-AN ZA bila kuwa KA-mi li.]

FEELINGS & EMOTIONS · Hisia na Machozi
• I feel calm, like things are okay. - Ninahisi utulivu, kana kwamba kila kitu ni sawa.  [NI-nahisi u-TU-li-vu, KA-na kwa-mba KI-la ki-tu ni SA-wa.]
• I’m shaking a little, I can’t hide it. - Ninatetemeka kidogo, siwezi kuficha.  [NI-na-te-te-mE-ka ki-dO-go, si-WE-zi ku-FI-cha.]
• My eyes are watery, I’m holding back. - Macho yangu yananilowa machozi, najaribu kujizuia.  [MA-cho ya-Ngu ya-na-ni-lo-wa MA-cho-zi, na-JA-ribu ku-JI-zu-a.]
• I feel heavy, like sadness is here. - Na-hisi uzito, kana kwamba huzuni imekaa hapa.  [NA-hisi u-ZI-to, KA-na kwa-mba hu-ZU-ni i-me-KAA ha-pa.]
• I just want to cry, quietly. - Nataka kulia, taratibu tu.  [NA-ta-ka ku-LI-a, ta-ra-ti-bu tu.]
• I feel relieved, the wait is over. - Nimepumua, kusubiri kumekwisha.  [NI-me-pu-MUA, ku-su-BI-ri ku-me-KWI-sha.]

CELEBRATIONS & PARTIES · Sherehe na Mikutano
• Cheers, happy birthday, let's celebrate! - Hongera, siku njema ya kuzaliwa, tuadhimishe!  [Hongera, siku NJEMA ya kuZALIWA, TUADHIMISHE!]
• I brought sparkling drinks for everyone. - Nimeleta vinywaji vyenye mng'ao kwa kila mtu.  [NIMEleta VI NYWAJI vyenye mNG'ao kwa KILA mtu.]
• Can we make a quick toast now? - Tunaweza kufanya toast fupi sasa hivi?  [TunaWEZA kuFANya toast FU PI sasa HIvi?]
• Who picked the playlist, it's perfect! - Ni nani aliyechagua nyimbo, ni nzuri kabisa!  [Ni NANI alieCHAGUA NYIMBO, ni nzuri KA BISA!]
• Where should I park for the event? - Ninaegesha wapi gari kwa ajili ya tukio?  [NinaEGEsha WAPI ga ri kwa ajili ya TU KIO?]
• I'll bring plates and napkins too. - Nitawaletea sahani na leso pia.  [NitaWAletea SAHANI na LESO pia.]
• Let's dance after the speeches. - Tucheze baada ya hotuba.  [TuCHEze baada ya hoTUBA.]

WORK & OFFICE · Kazi na Ofisi
• Where is the copy machine? - Kompyuta ya kunakili iko wapi?  [KOMpyuTA ya kuNAKili iKO wapi?]
• Can you share the updated schedule? - Unaweza kunitumia ratiba iliyosasishwa?  [UnaWEza kuNITUmia raTIBA iLIyoSAShwa?]
